name.text: Measures of Location and Dispersion Applications-q9

questiontext.text: The two methods of finding mode in a discrete series are: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

In the grouping method, the data is organized into intervals or classes (grouped frequency distribution), and you determine the mode within these intervals.

In the non-grouping method, you directly count the frequency of each individual value. You identify the value with the highest frequency as the mode. If there are multiple values with the same highest frequency, the dataset may be multimodal (having multiple modes).

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

Grouping and inspecting methods are used when calculating the mode in a discrete series, particularly when dealing with a large dataset that may have a wide range of values or when working with grouped frequency distributions. These methods are practical and more efficient for handling complex datasets.

[[/ if ]]
